description: Given an m x n matrix, return true if the matrix is Toeplitz. A matrix is Toeplitz if every diagonal from top-left to bottom-right has the same elements.
intuition: A Toeplitz matrix has the same value along every top-left to bottom-right diagonal. Simply check that each element equals the one diagonally above-left (mat[r][c] == mat[r-1][c-1]). If all such pairs match, the matrix is Toeplitz.
approach: For each cell (i, j) where i > 0 and j > 0, check if it equals the cell diagonally above-left (i-1, j-1). If any mismatch, return false.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: matrix = [[1,2,3,4],[5,1,2,3],[9,5,1,2]]

A Toeplitz matrix has all diagonals with the same value.
Check: each matrix[i][j] must equal matrix[i-1][j-1]

Row=1, Col=2: matrix[1][2]=2 vs matrix[0][1]=2 ✓

Row=2, Col=2: matrix[2][2]=1 vs matrix[1][1]=1 ✓
Row=2, Col=3: matrix[2][3]=2 vs matrix[1][2]=2 ✓

All checks pass → return true

If matrix[1][1] were 9 instead of 1:
Row=1, Col=1: 9 !== 1 → return false immediately
explanation:
1. A Toeplitz matrix requires all diagonal elements to be the same.
2. Check each cell against its upper-left diagonal neighbor.
3. If any cell differs from its diagonal predecessor, return False.
4. If all pass, return True.
hints: Each cell should equal its upper-left diagonal neighbor.
Check matrix[i][j] == matrix[i-1][j-1] for all valid i, j.
